what: Specs claims go test runs the copylocks check for you. It doesn't: copylocks is not in go test's default vet set, so a test run passes silently on this bug.
evidence: Page (Specs bubble): "go test runs this check of mine for you." Go 1.27.3 source, src/cmd/go/internal/test/test.go defaultVetFlags: "// \"-copylocks\"," is commented out. The enabled ones are atomic, bools, buildtag, directive, errorsas, ifaceassert, nilfunc, printf, slog, stdversion, stringintconv, tests. Scratch run on Go 1.27.3: a package with `func (c Counter) Inc()` (Counter holds a sync.Mutex) plus a test gives `go test` → PASS, while `go vet .` → "Inc passes lock by value: x.Counter contains sync.Mutex".
fix: Replace the sentence with: "go test doesn't run this check, so run go vet ./... yourself (or in CI)."

what: go vet's bubble says go test runs the lostcancel check automatically. It doesn't: lostcancel is not in go test's default vet set.
evidence: Page: "That's my lostcancel check. go test runs me too, automatically." Go 1.27.3 test.go defaultVetFlags has "// \"-lostcancel\"," commented out. Same scratch test as the ch25 finding: `ctx, _ := context.WithTimeout(...)` in a tested package. `go test` → PASS. `go vet .` → "the cancel function returned by context.WithTimeout should be called, not discarded, to avoid a context leak".
fix: "That's my lostcancel check. go test doesn't run it for you, so run go vet ./... before you commit."

what: The terminal shows exit code 1 for `go vet vet_many.go 2>&1 | sort -t: -k2,2n`, and the readlist teaches "exit code 1" from it. The command actually run had a hidden `; exit ${PIPESTATUS[0]}` appended. Typed as shown, the pipeline exits with sort's status, 0. The footer says "Commands are shown as typed" and doesn't disclose this.
evidence: /home/you/go-ch27/vet_many.cmd: shown "go vet vet_many.go 2>&1 | sort -t: -k2,2n", run "go vet vet_many.go 2>&1 | sort -t: -k2,2n; exit ${PIPESTATUS[0]}". data/go-ch27.json vet_many.go records exit 1. Page readlist: "No header, exit code 1 … Exit code 1 means it found something, so build scripts can stop." stdver.cmd's last step has the same kind of hidden suffix, "; (exit ${PIPESTATUS[0]})", but it doesn't change what's shown there (exit 0 either way).
fix: Smallest fix: drop data-exit from the panel 28 terminal, and change the readlist item to say that go vet on its own exits with 1 (the exit status of a pipeline is the last command's). Or show `set -o pipefail` as a visible step in the session. Then add one footer sentence about the PIPESTATUS suffixes.

what: The readlist says `defer stop()` lets a second Ctrl+C stop the program at once while it closes up. But a deferred stop runs only when main returns. Until then, further interrupts are still diverted to the context and do nothing.
evidence: Page: "defer stop() (line 13): Hands the signal back to the default: a second Ctrl+C now stops the program at once, for when closing up gets stuck." os/signal docs (Go 1.27.3 src/os/signal/signal.go): "Future interrupts received will not trigger the default (exit) behavior until the returned stop function is called … code should call stop as soon as the operations running in this Context complete". In signal_self.go, stop is only deferred (line 13), so it runs after "gate locked".
fix: "defer stop() (line 13): Hands the signal back to the default when main returns. To let a second Ctrl+C force-quit during closing up, call stop() right after <-ctx.Done() as well."

what: The lab says to remove the runtime.Gosched() line from race_count.go and run again. Doing exactly that doesn't compile, because "runtime" is then imported and not used.
evidence: Lab: "Then remove the runtime.Gosched() line and try again: how often does it go wrong now?" Scratch, Go 1.27.3: race_count.go with that line deleted → "./nopause.go:5:2: \"runtime\" imported and not used".
fix: "Then remove the runtime.Gosched() line and the \"runtime\" import (the Compiler will remind you), and try again …"

what: The lab experiment to see vet's lostcancel check doesn't work: `ctx, _ := context.WithTimeout(r.Context(), time.Second)` leaves ctx unused, so go vet stops at the type error and never reports lostcancel.
evidence: Lab: "Run go vet on your diner. Then change a handler to ctx, _ := context.WithTimeout(r.Context(), time.Second) and run it again." Scratch module, Go 1.27.3, greet handler with that line added: `go vet .` → "vet: ./main.go:11:2: declared and not used: ctx" (exit 1), with no lostcancel report.
fix: Use a line that also uses ctx, for example "ctx, _ := context.WithTimeout(r.Context(), time.Second); _ = ctx", or "…and pass ctx to something, such as fmt.Fprint(w, ctx.Err())".

what: "-ldflags isn't in the list" gives no reason, so readers will think Go never records -ldflags. It is missing only because this build used -trimpath. Without -trimpath, go version -m shows a "build -ldflags=…" line.
evidence: Page: "-ldflags isn't in the list: The recorded settings in this run don't mention it, so the version stamp is only in release." Go 1.27.3 src/cmd/go/internal/load/pkg.go: "if !cfg.BuildTrimpath { appendSetting(\"-ldflags\", ldflags) }". buildinfo.cmd builds with -trimpath.
fix: "-ldflags isn't in the list: with -trimpath, Go leaves the -ldflags setting out (it could contain paths); without -trimpath, go version -m shows it too."

what: Says a Mac binary runs "only on Macs with the same processor family". darwin/amd64 binaries also run on Apple-silicon Macs through Rosetta 2. Only the reverse (arm64 on Intel) fails.
evidence: Page: "'A binary built on my Mac runs on any Mac.' Only on Macs with the same processor family: darwin/arm64 and darwin/amd64 are different crates."
fix: "…darwin/arm64 and darwin/amd64 are different crates. An arm64 crate won't run on an Intel Mac; an amd64 crate runs on Apple silicon only through Apple's Rosetta translator."
